title: Bubbles scenario-manifest.json (v5.1 / M9)
description: Per-spec scenario-contract manifest. Lives at specs/<feature>/scenario-manifest.json. Records every Gherkin scenario with required-test-type, linked tests, evidence references, and lockdown status. Read by state-transition-guard.sh Check 3C (Gate G057). CANONICAL SHAPE IS THIS OBJECT. A legacy BARE TOP-LEVEL ARRAY of the same scenario objects also exists in the wild (5 manifests across downstream repos as of 2026-08-13) because the grep-based counter that predated the IMP-040 lints could not distinguish the two envelopes. Readers (scenario-obligation-lint.sh, test-mechanism-lint.sh, scenario-impact-resolve.sh) TOLERATE the bare array so those certified specs are not retroactively rejected, but it is NOT canonical and MUST NOT be produced by new work: a bare array carries no schemaVersion, so a future migration cannot detect which version it conforms to.

id.description: Stable scenario identifier (e.g. SCN-042-001). Persists across reword/renumber.

requiredTestType.description: Canonical test taxonomy classification — see agent-common.md.

linkedTests.description: Paths or test identifiers proving this scenario.

evidenceRefs.description: report.md anchors or tool-log session ids with raw output.

riskTier.description: OPTIONAL (IMP-040 SCOPE-7, COV-11). How much a wrong answer costs, which determines the strength of negative control the scenario owes. A uniform tier across every scenario carries no information; tier the ones that would actually hurt.

behaviorTraits.description: OPTIONAL (IMP-040 SCOPE-3, COV-9). The behavior traits this scenario actually has. bubbles.plan DERIVES the obligation set from these — see test-core.md 'Scenario Obligation Matrix'. Attaching every trait to every scenario is the failure mode this replaces, not a safe default: an always-identical set carries no information. Advisory and no-op unless declared; NOT part of required.

satisfiedBy.description: linkedTests references that discharge this obligation.

obligations.description: OPTIONAL (IMP-040 SCOPE-3, COV-9). The proof each declared behaviorTrait owes. One trait can imply several obligations, and a visible-UI assertion does not discharge a dependency-path one.

implementationRefs.description: OPTIONAL (IMP-040 SCOPE-9, REG-8). Repository-relative paths of the code path this scenario governs, plus the consumer surfaces it is observed through. Changed-spec validation intersects these with the diff so a change to a shared consumer marks every affected certified scenario for revalidation. Never inferred from filenames alone.

testMechanism.description: OPTIONAL (IMP-040 SCOPE-4, COV-10). HOW the linked test reaches and observes the behavior. The category label alone cannot prove path fidelity: an e2e-ui test can assert against hidden legacy DOM or invoke a renderer directly and still carry the label. The first four fields use CLOSED vocabularies so a claim is checkable rather than prose.

entrypoint.description: Where the test enters the system. `detached-renderer` proves a renderer unit, NOT route integration.

inputOrigin.description: Where the input comes from. Synthetic input may prove deterministic business logic; it cannot prove live acquisition.

assertionSurface.description: What the test asserts against. `hidden-dom` and `internal-state` may prove an internal projection, NOT a visible outcome.

dependencyPath.description: Which dependency state the test exercises. Shared vocabulary with the SCOPE-6 dependency-path coverage rules.

productionOwners.description: Repository-relative paths (and optional symbols when a code-index adapter is configured) of the production code that computes the asserted result.

negativeControl.description: The specific perturbation that makes this test fail. A test with no stated negative control has not been shown to be sensitive to the behavior it claims to prove.

negativeControlMechanism.description: OPTIONAL (IMP-040 SCOPE-7, COV-11). HOW the negative control is executed, ranked weakest to strongest. The scenario's riskTier sets the minimum: low accepts adversarial-input, medium requires at least perturbed-input, high requires mutation. The negative control must run through the production path.

negativeControlFallbackReason.description: OPTIONAL (IMP-040 SCOPE-7). Names why a weaker mechanism than the riskTier requires is being used, e.g. no mutation adapter is configured. Projects without mutation tooling use a weaker control until they opt in, but they state so explicitly rather than downgrading silently.

invariantRefs.description: OPTIONAL (IMP-106 SCOPE-3, DOM-LINEAGE). Domain-invariant ids from domainModel.invariants[].id (e.g. INV-REFUND-ONCE) that this scenario exercises. Links each SCN-* to the static business invariant(s) it proves, so lineage is answerable both directions (which test proves invariant X / which requirement justifies this scope). Advisory and no-op unless the repo declares a domainModel: block; NOT part of required.
